justifications.functional_suitability: While Fraud Scoring Engine scores transactions and Case Management & Rules Service provides case tools, there is no mechanism linking 'review' decisions to case storage. Additionally, Rule Authoring Engine updates AWS AppConfig, but Fraud Scoring Engine lacks any connection to load updated rules or models dynamically.
justifications.performance_efficiency: The sub-50ms P99 target at 3,000 TPS is well supported by Go/Rust in Fraud Scoring Engine, sub-millisecond feature reads from AWS ElastiCache (Redis), and asynchronous offloading of audit events via Amazon SQS. However, AWS API Gateway latency overhead under heavy load remains an unaddressed risk.
justifications.compatibility: AWS API Gateway provides standard HTTPS/JSON and gRPC endpoints to integrate with Payment Gateway / Merchants. S3 Batch Writer and Audit Logger interface cleanly with AWS S3 Object Lock and Amazon SQS using AWS SDK protocols.
justifications.usability: Fraud Analysts and Compliance Officers interact directly with the Case Workflow Controller over HTTPS/REST. Auditors / Regulators are provided secure compliance report access channels, satisfying the specified external user groups.
justifications.reliability: The architecture omits the critical R-07 requirement: there is no fallback, fail-open bypass, or circuit breaker in AWS API Gateway or Fraud Scoring Engine to prevent blocking payments when scoring is unavailable. SQS DLQ provides message fault tolerance, but payment availability targets are unaddressed.
justifications.security: Security is addressed with JWT Authorizer, Ingress Traffic Handler with AWS WAF, and Data Masking Proxy ensuring analysts never see unmasked PANs. In addition, S3 Batch Writer guarantees tamper-evident 7-year storage via AWS S3 with Object Lock. Tokenization services are not explicitly detailed.
justifications.maintainability: Clear container separation divides real-time scoring, analyst workflows, and audit persistence. Inside Fraud Scoring Engine, responsibilities are cleanly decoupled across API Controller, Feature Assembler, and Evaluation Core. AWS AppConfig isolates rule management, keeping operational overhead low for a three-engineer team.
justifications.portability: The design satisfies the AWS eu-west-1 target requirement. However, components are tightly coupled to AWS proprietary services (AWS API Gateway, AWS AppConfig, Amazon SQS, AWS S3 Object Lock), making portability to other cloud providers or on-premises environments difficult without significant refactoring.

PERF-01.justification: The Go/Rust scoring engine and ElastiCache feature store decouple audit writes asynchronously to SQS, enabling sub-50ms processing. However, AWS API Gateway latency overhead at P99 under 3,000 TPS requires careful tuning and regional optimization.
sensitivity_points: AWS API Gateway ingress overhead at 3,000 TPS
tradeoffs: Async audit dispatch via SQS preserves low latency over immediate write consistency

PERF-02.justification: Case management workloads are isolated in a separate container (Case Management & Rules Service) away from the scoring path. Analysts querying cases do not compete for resources with the Fraud Scoring Engine or ElastiCache, isolating peak scoring latency.
sensitivity_points: Physical isolation between analyst workloads and critical path scoring containers
tradeoffs: Separate microservices increase operational overhead for a small three-person team

AVAIL-01.justification: The architecture lacks a fallback or fail-open mechanism in AWS API Gateway if the Fraud Scoring Engine crashes. Without a secondary path or default decision engine, transactions will be dropped or fail during an outage rather than recovering within 1 minute.
sensitivity_points: Single point of failure at the scoring engine ingress
tradeoffs: Failing closed protects against fraud but risks blocking legitimate payments during crashes

AVAIL-02.justification: Audit events are emitted asynchronously via SQS and buffered away from the scoring execution path. A sluggish or unavailable S3 target only impacts the Audit Worker and queues, protecting scoring latency and preventing record loss via DLQs.
sensitivity_points: SQS retention window and DLQ durability during prolonged S3 outages
tradeoffs: Eventual consistency of audit records in exchange for guaranteed scoring availability

MOD-01.justification: The Fraud Scoring Engine includes an Evaluation Core, but provides no mechanism for dynamic model loading, traffic splitting, rollback, or model version tagging. A model deployment requires a full container redeployment with unstated rollback and versioning mechanics.
sensitivity_points: Container deployment coupling for machine learning model updates
tradeoffs: Compiled binaries maximize scoring throughput but impede rapid, zero-downtime model swaps

MOD-02.justification: The Rule Authoring Engine connects to AWS AppConfig, but no relationship or data flow connects AppConfig or the Case Management container to the Fraud Scoring Engine. The scoring engine lacks a documented channel to ingest updated rules dynamically at runtime.
sensitivity_points: Missing configuration synchronization path between rules service and scoring engine
tradeoffs: Centralized configuration management requires robust synchronization channels to runtime nodes

SEC-01.justification: The Data Masking Proxy explicitly masks PAN data for analysts, ensuring card numbers are not exposed. However, the design omits intrusion detection, behavioral monitoring, or automated alerting mechanisms to detect anomalous account access within 15 minutes.
sensitivity_points: Absence of real-time security analytics and behavioral anomaly detection
tradeoffs: Masking protects data confidentiality but does not address credential compromise detection

SEC-02.justification: Audit trails are preserved using S3 Object Lock and Glacier Deep Archive for 7 years in immutable, tamper-evident format. Auditors and compliance officers have designated export and reporting channels to reproduce decision records and explanations on demand.
elements: AWS S3 with Object Lock and Glacier Deep Archive
sensitivity_points: S3 Object Lock retention policy configuration over a 7-year lifecycle
tradeoffs: Glacier retrieval latency requires retrieval requests to complete within one working day
